params.why: every instance ends with a genuine simplification, so the last step is never a no-op

stem: Write the recurring decimal ${=n}.{=t}\dot{{=c}}$ as a single fraction in simplest form (not a mixed number). The dot marks the digit that repeats for ever; the digits before it do not repeat.
solution: Write the decimal out as an equation: $x = {=n}.{=dec}\ldots$
Multiply both sides by ${=base}$ so that the decimal point sits just before the recurring digit: ${=base}x = {=low}.{=tail}\ldots$
Multiply both sides by ${=base2}$ to move the decimal point one place further, past one recurring digit: ${=base2}x = {=high}.{=tail}\ldots$

Subtract the equation for ${=base}x$ from the equation for ${=base2}x$ so that the recurring digits cancel: ${=base2}x - {=base}x = ({=high}.{=tail}\ldots) - ({=low}.{=tail}\ldots)$, which gives ${=bot}x = {=top}$.
Simplify: the highest common factor of ${=top}$ and ${=bot}$ is ${=g}$, so $x = \frac{{=ans_n}}{{=ans_d}}$.
notes: The book's twist, as in 11-6e (12.27 with the last 7 recurring, solved by 100x - 10x = 90x = 1105, giving 221/18) and 12b (0.6 then 3 recurring): non-recurring digit(s) between the point and the recurring digit, so TWO multiplications (10^m and 10^(m+1)) before subtracting, plus a whole-number part and a compulsory simplification. m (1 or 2 non-recurring digits) only changes the two powers of ten; the steps are identical. The recurring digit is 1 to 8 (0 would terminate, 9 is the 0.9-recurring trap) and must differ from the digit just before it, so the printed form is never the redundant one the book itself uses for 11-6e (12.27 followed by a recurring 7 is the same number as 12.2 followed by a recurring 7; my solution would be correct for either reading, but the stem avoids the ambiguity). First non-recurring digit is non-zero so no leading-zero display. Algebra: 10^(m+1)x - 10^m x = 9*10^m x = (9*low + c), where low is the whole part and non-recurring digits read as one integer. Check on the book's number: n=12, t=2, c=7, m=1 gives 90x = 1105, 221/18. 7110 instances after g > 1; all checked by script (fraction equals the decimal to 45 places, fraction is in lowest terms and is never an integer).
